jp: 弟[おとうと]{は|wa-topic}毎日[まいにち]バス{で|de-means}学校[がっこう]{に/へ|ni-destination}行[い]きます。
en: My younger brother goes to school by bus every day.
why: The place he heads for takes に (or へ); まで would mean 'as far as' school.

jp: 父[ちち]{は|wa-topic}夜[よる]十一時[じゅういちじ]{まで|made-until}テレビ{を|o-object}見[み]ています。
en: My father watches TV until eleven at night.
why: まで marks the time up to which the activity continues; に would just point to eleven o'clock.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]{の|no-possessive}家[いえ]{まで|made-until}自転車[じてんしゃ]{で|de-means}三十分[さんじゅっぷん]かかります。
en: It takes thirty minutes by bicycle to my grandmother's house.
why: かかる measures the distance up to the end point, which is marked by まで.

jp: 姉[あね]{は|wa-topic}毎週[まいしゅう]日曜日[にちようび]、実家[じっか]{に/へ|ni-destination}帰[かえ]ります。
en: My older sister goes back to her parents' home every Sunday.
why: The place she returns to takes に (or へ); まで would mean 'as far as'.

jp: 今夜[こんや]{は|wa-topic}父[ちち]{が|ga-subject}帰[かえ]る{まで|made-until}起[お]きています。
en: Tonight I'll stay up until my father comes home.
why: まで after a verb gives the point when the waiting ends; に and へ cannot follow a plain verb here.

jp: 犬[いぬ]{を|o-object}庭[にわ]{に/へ|ni-destination}出[だ]しました。
en: I let the dog out into the garden.
why: The garden is where the dog ends up, so に (or へ) is right; まで would mean 'as far as the garden'.
